evidence_items.locator: AI-generated Child Sexual Abuse Videos: 2025 Data and Trends, second paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: IWF assessed 3,443 realistic AI-generated abuse videos in 2025, versus 13 in 2024. Its accompanying observations include fabricated videos of known victims, establishing substantial harmful impersonation rather than merely benign synthetic production.

evidence_items.locator: FAQ, What is the growth rate of deepfakes?
evidence_items.explanation: A combined database of media-reported incidents shows broader growth after the post. It combines audio, images and videos and is sensitive to news coverage, so it cannot independently establish the video-specific outcome.

The researchers examine how video-generation models enable nonconsensual intimate imagery. This supports the technological connection, but supplies neither a worldwide longitudinal count nor attribution to Sora itself.

unresolved_gaps: No comprehensive, consistently measured worldwide series of deceptive AI-generated videos was established.
Observed counts can change with detection effort, reporting and platform visibility.
The decisive comparison covers child sexual abuse videos; it does not measure growth across every deepfake category.
The evidence does not establish how much of the increase was produced with Sora.
